task:
Mission? Well, look straight ahead. Now give me a jump... higher! Even higher! One step forward. Squat down, stand up straight. One jump forward, one jump back - don't turn! Stand up, stop wincing and nursing your tail base... Not bad at all.

I think you are the one we need, <Ranger>. Our scholars invented a unique device, which was sent to the Institute of Inventions and Innovations on planet <ToPlanet> for patenting. Unfortunately, we didn't have time to test it thoroughly so now we can't complete the application for the patent. There is only one test remaining - field-testing - but it is the most important one. We have already rented a test lab in the Institute and invited stuntmen but they failed to complete the testing.

As a ranger, you must be perfectly trained. We will even pay you twice as much as a stuntman gets - it makes <Money> cr, if you go to planet <ToPlanet> (system <ToStar>) and manage to test the device. But keep in mind that the patent submission is due to expire, so you must do all the testing by <Date>.
success: It's just wonderful, that you helped the scholars from IIII to finish the "Jumper"'s testing, and now they can devote all their time to the "Runner"'s development. Tell us where we can find you so when the device is ready, we will know who to ask to test it. So, where can we find you? Alright... What a strange name for a system - sounds like an ancient Maloq swearword... Pooh! How can a ranger be such a can?! Here are your <Money> credits - you deserved them. Good bye, <Ranger>.
loc.2.0:
- You must test the jumping backpack - "Jumper". We rented a pavilion for the testing and tossed a facility. Your task is to go through the labyrinth made of hanging platforms jumping from one platform to another using the "Jumper". The labyrinth consists of the starting and finishing points and five rows of platforms between them. <clr> Your task is to make a number of jumps to get from the starting point through the labyrinth to the finishing point <clrEnd>. And you can jump only within the row you are at or onto the platforms of the next row.

Jumps require power consumption, which is measured in ergo and depends on the length of the jump. You will have <clr>two batteries <clrEnd> <clr>20 ergo<clrEnd> each. One battery is active, and the other is spare. Our technicians promise that would be enough.

There are additional devices somewhere on the platforms, which allow you to replace the active battery, top it up or even get back to the starting point where you can charge the both batteries and start the testing from the very beginning. If you want to cancel the testing and, accordingly, abandon your fee, you can use the emergency return button.
loc.2.1:
Instead of answering Hab pointed to the window opening to the testing pavilion. There were half a dozen of platforms about two meters in diameter each hanging behind the window at a height of almost 20 meters. The distance between them was from 2 to 10 meters. The platforms were white with one coloured stripe along the edge.

- There are five rows of platforms here, each row is marked with a certain colour. The technicians changed the configuration many times already making the facility easier and safer, so I have only general information about its structure: 
<clr>- Starting point<clrEnd>
<clr>- Yellow row<clrEnd> - 4 platforms
<clr>- Red row<clrEnd> - 4 platforms
<clr>- Violet row<clrEnd> - 5 platforms, plus one battery charger
<clr>- Blue row<clrEnd> - 4 platforms, the teleport can be used here
<clr>- Green row<clrEnd> - 3 platforms, the teleport is active here too
<clr>- Final point<clrEnd> - the testing is over here.

I would advise you to drag your heels here and study the facility's structure first. When you reach the <clr>Green<clrEnd> or <clr>Blue<clrEnd> row, you will be able to return to the starting point, charge your batteries and do the testing from the beginning. But note - you can do it just once.
loc.2.2:
- This is a portable device for impulse transfers at short distances, or a jumping backpack, - saying this, he pointed to something that really looked like a backpack. - It looks like a jet or antigravitational backpack, - the professor explained, - but it requires notably less power. It allows you to jump 10-15 times better than you are able to. The oversensitive membrane picks up the fibres of a nerve contraction while a command signal is running from the little brain to...
- Can you make it clearer? 
- In general, it can help you jump further and higher with no effort. Take a run, push yourself off the ground - and by-y-ye. And then...you are either lucky or not. Though there are some problems with aiming as well as while calculating the necessary strength of the jump at some distances but there should be some element of hazard that adds salt to the flight! Along with that, we installed an automatic gyroscopic compensator into the backpack.
- What if you have a kangaroo or a Venerian jumpling wear this thing? I bet the animal will be surprised.
- Come on... The ceilings will be dirty. Though I admit it's a rather interesting idea. Do you happen to have a pet baby kangaroo? It's a pity... I wonder what will happen if we have a 5 ton elephant or a bellypotamus wear the backpack? It's going to be a damn massive weapon!
- Rather a flattening massive weapon, - you specified.
loc.2.3:
- There were some... But there is no science without sacrifice; you must know it! Naturally, nothing was left to accident! We have a permanent first aid on duty with everything necessary for cremating and we even found a donor with your blood group! If you are religious, we have priests of all main Galaxy faiths. At last, we have your address if we need to send 10 000 credits according to the insurance....
- Well, that was comforting...
- But fatal accidents are very rare, especially now that we put huge mattresses under the platforms.
- Do you think that's enough? - you asked acidly.
- Don't you think so? Alright, we'll put one more mattress there. But try to keep it clean... And by the way - after each failure... well, we reconfigured the facility's structure after each failure, making it safer. The last took stuntmen didn't come to harm at all except for the Maloq who decided to pass the last two meters with a spent battery. Such "deeds" force our technicians to grease the platforms' edges...
loc.2.4:
Depending on the length of the jump, the power consumption will be the following:

<clr>2<clrEnd> meters - [p10] ergo 
<clr>3-4<clrEnd> meters - [p11] ergo
<clr>5<clrEnd> meters - [p12] ergo
<clr>6-7<clrEnd> meters - [p13] ergo
<clr>8<clrEnd> meters - [p14] ergo
<clr>9-12<clrEnd> meters - [p15] ergo

Our technicians promise that 40 ergo will be enough to go through the labyrinth. You are given <clr>two batteries <clrEnd> <clr>20 ergo<clrEnd> each. Only one battery can be active - its power is used for the jump. But you can replace the battery with the help of the special device - there are such samples in the test labyrinth.
loc.2.5:
- In the first place, you can <clr>replace the active battery with the spare one <clrEnd> on every <clr>platform with an even number <clrEnd> and use it for jumping.
Secondly, there is a charger installed on <clr>the central platform of the Violet row <clrEnd> - it adds <clr>12 ergo<clrEnd> to the active battery automatically.
Thirdly, there is an accelerator on <clr>the first platform <clrEnd> of some row, I can't remember now which one. It will transfer you onto the first platform of the next sector just for <clr>1 ergo<clrEnd>. 
And of course, we will provide you with a portable <clr>teleport<clrEnd>, which will help you to return to the starting point where you will be able to charge the both batteries and start from the beginning. But it's <clr>disposable<clrEnd> and can be used only on the platforms of the <clr>Blue<clrEnd> and <clr>Green<clrEnd> rows!
loc.2.6:
- You must go through the test labyrinth made of hanging platforms wearing this thing and jumping from one platform to another. The labyrinth consists of the starting and finishing points and five rows of platforms between them.. <clr> Your task is to make a number of jumps to get from the starting point through the labyrinth to the finishing point<clrEnd>. Along with this, you can jump only within the row you are at or onto the platforms of the next row. So it's not that easy!
 
You will have <clr>two batteries <clrEnd> - active and spare <clr>20 ergo<clrEnd> each. Note that the power consumption depends on the distance length! Don't forget to use the additional devices installed in the labyrinth. 

You will be provided with a disposable teleport only - it will help you to get back to the starting point, where you can charge the batteries and start from the beginning. So you may grow familiar with the labyrinth at first. Emergency return will mean that you cancel the testing and abandon your <Money> cr.
loc.4.0: You banged the door proudly and left the IIII... You didn't earn anything but health before wealth.
loc.5.0:
The professor wished you good luck and blessed you. Then he took you to the test pavilion.
- Note that the battery replacement devices are installed on the even platforms of each sector. Here is a portable teleport adjusted to return back here. You can use it only once - while passing the labyrinth' last two rows. The emergency return button means that you cancel the testing of just can't complete it. And in case of any accidents - well, you understand what I mean, mind your language and don't dirty the floor - our young ladies assisting in the lab have such a weak stomach.

You went up the stairs to the starting point. Meanwhile the professor and a dozen of his associates were making bets what platform you will fall from. 
"Snooks, lab rats", - you got furious and came to the edge. It is high! Round 20 meters, so the fall will be short but very painful. Well, you must jump. Which sector will you choose?
loc.5.1:
You transferred to the starting point. The professor ran to you and hooked up the charger to the batteries:
- So, did you manage to study the labyrinth well enough? Note, you have no more chances to return. And we are pressed for time - we need to format the report, attach it to the application form, register and queue to the acceptance committee. Hurry up, please. You are not the only one after <Money> credits. Honestly, I don't cherish high hopes that you will be a success. The technicians must have done something wrong again reconfiguring the facility. Though they swear that the labyrinth is passable...

You reassured the scholar that you would manage it by all means and got ready for the first jump...
loc.6.0: You landed softly onto the platform, which didn't even vibrate. There were a lot of footprints of all possible shapes and sizes - from sneakers to huge bare Maloq heels.
loc.6.1:
There were a lot of footprints of all possible shapes and sizes on the platform - from sneakers to huge bare Maloq heels.
"I am no worse" - you thought and decided to put yourself on record. After many fruitless and rather painful attempts to imprint your foot on the platform, you just used your blaster to poker a 58-64-size footprint with your name - <Ranger> - inside and were satisfied.
loc.7.0: After landing on the nearest platform, you all but stepped on the banana peel left there by some unknown prankster. What you said was not wishing him health and wealth.
loc.7.1: After you all but stepped on the banana peel again, you took a fresh and ripe quanga - a gift from a Menzol friend - cut it to small pieces and put them accurately along the platform edge. Who knows, may be, they'll notice your contribution too.
loc.8.0:
You hit your heels on the platform nastily and groaned with pain. There was an inscription along the very edge of the platform scratched with some sharp thing:
"Ranger Bob was here. <CurDate>"

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.8.1:
" Ranger Bob was here <CurDate>", - you saw that inscription for the second time already and these simple words awoke your creativity. Soon a new inscription spread along the platform:
"And ranger <Ranger> was here twice. <CurDate>!"

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.9.0:
You landed softly on the platform and all but hit your nose on the battery replacement device. There was a tablet hanging on the device:
"Do not jump off the platform!" 
Some prankster replaced "j" with "h".
loc.9.1:
You landed softly on the platform and all but hit your nose on the battery replacement device again. There were familiar words on the tablet:
"Do not jump off the platform!" 
Some prankster replaced "j" with "h".

You are a man of humour; so it didn't take you long to modify the inscription and replace "off" with "on":
"Don't jump on the platform!"
It went without saying that you left the previous modification unchanged.
loc.10.0:
You landed on the platform and all but slip in a small pool of blood. You looked down from the platform and saw another pool, much bigger in size. Several teeth were drifting on the red surface. You felt sick and thought about your mom.

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.11.0:
This time you were down on your luck - you had to use your hands, feet, and teeth to miss falling down from the 20 meters height. But then your nails and teeth left clear scratches on the platform. The next test man will be surprised to see 60 neat scores on the platform. 
"By the way, why 60?" - you thought and started counting...
loc.11.1: You were surprised to notice space-boot prints and clear scratches left by nails and teeth on the platform. And these were 60 deep scores! You tried to fit your foot with the prints and were proud of your abilities - the scores on the platform looked quite impressive! Selenite crowns deserve their reputation.
loc.12.0:
All that you found on the platform were some spit traces, an empty Cola can, and a scratched inscription:
"Bob's drunk a lot and ate a little here". And the can was giving a strong alcoholic odour by the way.
loc.12.1:
Souse traces (some spits, an empty Cola can giving an alcoholic odour, and an scratched inscription: " Bob's drunk a lot and ate a little here ") kept exciting envy of all individuals jumping by.

"Ah, Bambay in your dreams, you damned drunkard. A hungry gobzaurus for your birthday from your mother-in-low, or a penchequack in heat", - you felt envious and surprised by your own cruelty. See what frequent visits to the Faeyan planets can do along with seeing booze in the unofficial magazines only.
loc.13.0:
A soft fall with a roll and a roar of a parturient gobzaurus - you all but fell off the platform that turned out to be surprisingly slippery. You could hardly hold up and saw that the platform had a bad list.

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.13.1:
You still remembered about the bad list so managed to hold up.

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.14.0:
You managed to group yourself in the air and it saved your life. This was the only reason why the iron-sided 57-sized boot lost by an unknown Maloq didn't knock the stuffing out of you when you fell on it.

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.14.1:
After one more bang against the iron-sided 57-sized boot, you kicked it hastily trying to fling it down the platform. About ten minutes passed before the pain and tears had gone and then you examined the boot and saw that it was entered rather deeply into the surface of the platform. It was only then that you noticed that the platform was hanging a couple of meters lower than the rest of them.
"Now you tell me, brother, what strength is", - you scratched your head thoughtfully.

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.15.0:
Hardly had you landed onto the platform, an automated voice said:
"Active battery, current charge - {[p2]-12} ergo. Boost charging function is active. Boost charging complete. Active battery, current charge - [p2] ergo"

"Heh, I wish my spaceship had such a battery", - you thought enviously.
loc.16.0:
"Down we dive, spouting our flame from under off with one hell-of-a-roar..." - you landed gracefully onto the platform.

- Well, I got skill, I got experience. Come on let's twist again, like we did last su-u-u-ummer!!! - you were squalling contentedly but then gave it a thought and changed one word: - Come on let's jump again...!
loc.17.0:
The platform was flying at you. You tried to remember some prayers but only nasty stories and recipes of the Maloq cuisine came to your mind. You were lucky though and escaped just with fright and injured manhood - fortunately, no self-maiming.

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.18.0: After landing onto the platform, you gave it a thought - you had already jumped rather far. And by the way, the professor never mentioned anything about the call of nature. Only after jumping with the "Jumper" you realised where adrenaline comes from.
loc.18.1:
You landed and looked at the charge indicator - you had {[p2]+[p4]+[p5]+1} ergo left.
"Well, three-four more accurate jumps, and the torture will be over for today, - you cheered up. - And just one inaccurate. Then the torture will be over for ever. Who will take my spaceship and tricks, I wonder? Damn it. As soon as I'm back, I must make my will..."
loc.19.0:
After you slammed on the platform, you realised what problems make the life of grasshoppers, fleas and jumpawaiians so hard and short. They pull such stunts one hundred times per day.

The portable teleport started peeping on your belt. That meant it was active. It will help you to return to the starting point to charge the batteries and  - good luck again!
There is a battery replacement device here too.
loc.19.1:
If your memory serves you well, last time you thought about grasshoppers' fate right on this place. Grasshoppers are nothing compared to you! They don't have to simultaneously gauge the difference in the cost of luxury goods on Aldeeb and Venus.  Try to explain to some Rachekhan's offspring that the only cargo for sale in your hold are beam weapons and Maloq coffins and you would be happy to share them in this particular order. Lucky insects - they continually eat and crap everywhere. Nothing else!.

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.20.0:
"Boeing 737 is landing, please clear the runway. Please clear the runway..." - you snuffled trying to boo a stupid bird that sat right on your way. The bird noticed the UFO and decided to win the mastery in the air. Actually, it hurt you a lot pecking such a doughty person on the noble nose. But after that she tired of you and the landing went smoothly.

The portable teleport started peeping on your belt. That meant it was active. It will help you to return to the starting point to charge the batteries and  - good luck again!
loc.20.1:
This time the bird disappeared but you still managed to land right into the sticky and sickly traces of its presence there.
"What did she steal from the institute canteen, I wonder? - you thought and pinched your nose. - It must have been Peleng soup "hoosh-moosh", which is used as a ratting means by other races..."
loc.21.0:
After landing onto the very edge of the platform, you saw a scratched inscription:
"Bob was h..." - after "h" it was chopped and a long deep scar along with five minor ones stretched to the edge of the platform.

The portable teleport started peeping on your belt. That meant it was active. It will help you to return to the starting point to charge the batteries and  - good luck again!
loc.21.1:
You landed near the familiar inscription "Bob was h..." and spent a few minutes immortalising your deed:
"<Ranger> have been here. I have also been there, and there. And I'm going to jump there.... On the whole, I've been here twice!"
loc.22.0:
"Ouch!"
The landing was abysmal this time - your feet were burning like on fire, and your completely new space-boots with magnetic soles squished softly and decided to go their own way, bit by bit - the sole of the right boot flew off to the right with a subtle whizz.

The portable teleport started beeping on your belt. That meant it was active. It will help you to return to the starting point to charge the batteries and  - good luck again!
There is a battery replacement device here too.
loc.22.1:
Considering your previous experience, you managed to land onto the platform smoothly. You stepped on the edge and noticed your boot sole on the floor. There was a pair of strike-me-pink-sized sneakers and a completely chewed up Addid-Ace shoe - the label adored by professional pilots and gobzaurus hunters. By the look of thing, the shoe's owner was neither a pilot, nor a good hunter.

There is a battery replacement device here.
loc.23.0: This time you jumped not very far, but obviously high, as high as to raise a bump banging on the pavilion's ceiling. But you paid off and managed to scratch a swear word on the ceiling and unscrewed a neon lightbulb out of the lamp.
loc.23.1: You admired your masterpiece with all the pride sailing up to the ceiling. This time it was not just a swearword that you managed to scratch but a whole poem written by your drunken friend Harry long ago. Even Maloq pirates of the blackest dye redden with embarrassment when they hear it. You were too modest to sign your name in the end and just wrote: "Corsair Santa Clause. Happy New Year, freaks!"
loc.24.0: "We are the cha-a-ampions, my friend..." - you sang with your hands tightened desperately on the edge of the platform. You turned out to be lucky because otherwise you would have been groaning inarticulately twenty metres lower from here. Inhale! Exhale! Now you threw yourself over the edge and crawled away from the inviting depth.
loc.24.1: So you are here again. The Green row is the last one. Why did they paint the last row green, you wonder? It would have been more logical to make it red - most of the accidents happen here. On the other side, if most of the testers were Pelengs with green blood, this colour is matching.
loc.25.0:
You landed onto the platform and signed with relief - you almost reached the final point - it was close at hand. Rather hairy hand, one should say because only a Maloq hand is attached to a two-meter arm.

"Come on, baby, just two meters, try to pass those last two meters..." - you sang rephrasing the famous song about a lustful Maloq.
loc.25.1:
And there was your chance, so near, oh so near. It's final point already. One more successful jump - and you are there. If you are a little bit down on your luck, you'll know what they serve in the institute's sick ward. And if it is a bad luck, you'll be able to play genii - you'll be cremated, your ashes will be put in a jug...sorry, in a urn. Some Charley will open it up in tree hundred years and you'll say: 
"I'm all ears and ready to obey, my lord. Shall I break your ribs or train your mother-in-law?" 
Heh, dreaming again!.
loc.26.0:
Your last jump was unbelievably beautiful - a storm of applause came from underneath and in the last moment you realised that the crowd of on-lookers will soon turn into the crowd of victims because you were landing right on their heads. Fortunately, everything turned out well and nobody was hurt.

- At last! - the professor was shaking your hand in excitement. - We thought we would have to cancel the project due to excess life and health risk. The rectorate started to look awry at us when we receive the bills for the medicine. You deserved your award, <Ranger>, all you need to do now is to get back to your employer on the <ToPlanet> planet to take it. By the way, I want to thank you personally.
- What for?
- Don't you understand? I staked half of my yearly salary on you if you go through the labyrinth! By the way, do you want to pocket a little bit more?
loc.34.0: You pushed the urgent teleport button and landed in the lab in a minute. A whole crowd of scholars were looking at you with disappointment. The Maloq on crutches was also there. He gave you a cheerful nod and pointed to his broken leg as if saying: "It would have been much worse, lad". You agreed with him all in all and hurried to you spaceship ignoring the annoyed scholars.
loc.35.0:
- Well, let's go.
The professor brought you to the neighbouring pavilion. Really, there turned out to be two platforms hanging at the height of 3 meters with several spheres over each. The scholar gave you a special gauge-feeler and charged the active battery to [p10] <clr>ergo<clrEnd>. The charger indicator flickered. Hab sighed sadly:
- Note, <Ranger>, you are our last hope of the successful device display in front of the commission. Financial and energetic resources of the project are exhausted. Mind your award in the amount of <clr>1000<clrEnd> cr - I'm sure this will help you. Choose the platform. You can simply go to another one any time, so your choice is not of much importance. There is a battery replacement device on each platform but don't forget to look to the charge level and remember that after the first battery replacement [p12] <clr>ergo<clrEnd> will move to the activated battery.
loc.38.0:
Hmph. Air is not your cup of tea. Space vacuum is easier to harness. You failed to supply the device with enough power to display it but we can prepare the patent application form without it. Though I understand that 1000 cr wouldn't have been redundant.

After shaking hands with the professor and giving the unblessed device a farewell kick, you left the IIII building and returned to the spaceport. And you skirted all holes, puddles and stones on your way - even the smallest ones.
loc.42.0:
You are standing on the second platform in the prime testing room. There are several replenishing spheres hanging over you at different height. And there used to be much more of them here - one can see several broken bars on the ceiling that obviously used to hold similar spheres. You saw such a bar in the corridor - it was wound around a Maloq ranger's hand instead of a bracelet.

<clr>Active<clrEnd> battery's charge is [p2] ergo
<clr>Spare<clrEnd> battery's charge is {[p4]+[p5]+1} ergo
<clr>You need to add<clrEnd> {39-([p2]+[p4]+[p5])} ergo to the battery.
loc.43.0:
You are standing on the first platform in the prime testing room. There are several replenishing spheres hanging over you at different height. You can see a lot of prints left by fingers, hands and even feet. As for the floor...well, nothing else could be expected considering the number of cripples in the institute's corridors.

The charge of the <clr>active<clrEnd> battery is [p2] ergo
The charge of the <clr>spare<clrEnd> battery is {[p4]+[p5]+1} ergo
<clr>You need to add<clrEnd> {39-([p2]+[p4]+[p5])} ergo to the batteries.
loc.47.0:
You managed to supply the device with enough power to display it. The professor was glad to tell you 1000 cr - now the "Jumper" will be presented to the commission in all its glory.

After shaking hands with the professor, you left the IIII building and returned to the spaceport. And you skirted all holes, puddles and stones on your way - even the smallest ones.
loc.50.0:
You took an aerocab that brought you to the Inventions and Innovations. It was near the Academy of Anthropological and Amorphous Anomalies. You entered and asked which way you should go.

A gloomy assistant accompanied you along the tortuous corridors. You met a Maloq with a stunt man's badge hopping with his crutches, then they carried by a litter with an unconscious man - your colleague. A gaal in a wheelchair saw where you were going. Then he approached you, gave you a sympathising look, and mentioned quietly: "Heh, he's so young", - after that he wheeled away.

The assistant brought you to the "Test laboratory No 13" and kindly opened the door.
- <Ranger>? - a fae stood up to meet you. - Nice to meet you, I'm professor Hab, I manage the testing of the device and collect all the information necessary for the patent application preparation. Have a sit.
You sat obediently on the offered chair.
- Stand up, now sit down again. Bounce on your toes. Higher. Still higher! Now hold your breath. Hold your left ear with your right hand and the right ear with your left hand... Not mine!!!
He measured your pulse and nodded with satisfaction.
- Excellent. Pulse, co-ordination, reflexes  - you are in perfect shape and this is very important for the "Jumper"'s testing. By the way, you may breathe.

You exhaled with relief:
loc.50.1: - See, it's very simple. And even not scary at all if you don't look down or close your eyes, which I don't recommend. Otherwise we'll have problems catching you or looking for a new volunteer. Plus I bet, you'll be cursing if you tumble and I hate cursors - we dealt with such an ill-bred Maloq today... Do you have any more questions?
loc.50.2: - This is elementary, the most important thing is to cut it fine estimating the battery charge. Timely battery replacement will also help a lot. This is why our requirements to the test men's intelligence are very high. It's understandable, that you also must remember about the power consumption for each jump - if you don't reach the final point, the test will be a failure. So, are you ready or do you have any more questions?
loc.50.3: - But I must warn you beforehand - if you fail and tumble, don't forget that you are a ranger, keep your emotions - there are women here. And don't you think that your relatives will have no problems getting the 10 000 insurance - <ToPlanet>'s bureaucrats became geniuses in their art. Do you have any more questions?
loc.52.0:
- Not at all. It's just additional money. You will get your <Money> credits for sure but you can also earn a little bit more...
- How far is this "more" and what do I need to do?
- See, I'm sure the commission will want to watch the device operating. After you found the best route, any assistant can manage it. Furthermore, your fee is so...formidable that we can't hire you to go through the labyrinth again. But there is one problem - the batteries are spent. I'd like to request you to use one of the first configurations of the testing facility <clr>to charge the batteries to the maximum <clrEnd>, and I'll pay you <clr>1000<clrEnd> cr. But at first you'll have to jump with the "Jumper" a little bit. You lose nothing and can get some profit - what would you say?
loc.53.0: You left the building of IIII and went to the spaceport. You were very slow and careful going to the aerocab rank and skirted even the smallest puddles and stones.
loc.54.0:
- Wonderful! Here, I'm giving you a battery <clr> with <clrEnd> [p10] <clr>ergo<clrEnd>. The configuration consists of two platforms connected by a bridge with spheres over it. Every time you touch such a sphere with a special gauge-feeler, you add a certain amount of ergo to the battery's charge. But the height of the spheres is different - this is a testing facility for the "Jumper" - so you'll spend some power on the jump. Not only must you compensate the consumption but also <clr>charge the batteries to 20 ergo each<clrEnd>
- How much power do I spend on one jump?
- The spheres are fixed on a certain height:
<clr>2 meters<clrEnd> require [p10] ergo;
